clips.asr_text: Today's topic is After 20 Years.
This story follows two old friends whose lives take different paths. After many years apart, can their friendship still hold?
Listen for why Bob is waiting at this place tonight.
Bob and Jimmy promised to meet here twenty years later. Will Jimmy show up?
Bob has finally met the man he believes is Jimmy, but then he suddenly pulls away. What has made him stop?
Sheltered from the rain.
protected from the rain in a place where it cannot reach you.
Pull it down.
To make a standing structure fall or be removed.
Plainclothes officer.
A police officer who wears ordinary clothes instead of a uniform.

Bob stood in the doorway of a closed hardware store, sheltered from the rain. It was almost ten. He shifted his unlit cigar between his teeth and looked down the street. Twenty years was a long time, but he had not forgotten the place. A patrolman stopped beside him.
Just waiting for a friend.
Bob explained.
There used to be a restaurant here.
They pulled it down five years ago.
Bob struck a match. The flame lit his face as he raised it to his cigar.
We had our last dinner there twenty years ago tonight. My best friend, Jimmy. We grew up together, like brothers.
The patrolman listened calmly while rain tapped against the pavement.
I went west.
Bob continued.
Jimmy stayed here. He thought New York was the only place worth living. Before we parted, we promised to meet here at ten tonight, whatever happened.
Have you heard from him?
Not for years. We lost touch.
Bob smiled.
Still, a promise meant something to Jimmy. He'll come if he's alive.
How long will you wait?
Half an hour.
Well, I hope he turns up. Good night.

The patrolman walked on. Bob leaned against the doorway, listening for footsteps. Once he took out his watch, then slipped it away again. He had traveled too far to worry about a few minutes. At half past ten, a tall man in a long overcoat hurried towards him.
Is that you, Bob?
Jimmy!

The man caught both his hands. Bob laughed with relief. For a moment, they seemed young again, with their whole lives ahead of them. They set off, arm in arm. Bob talked eagerly about the West, his business, and the money he had made. After twenty years, there was almost too much to say. Then they passed a drugstore. Light from its windows fell across their faces. Bob stopped and pulled his arm free.
You're not Jimmy. Twenty years can change a man, but not the shape of his nose.
They can change a good man into a bad one.
The tall man replied.
You're under arrest, Bob. You're wanted in Chicago.
Bob stared at him.
Before we go, there is a note for you.
Bob unfolded it under the bright window.

Bob, it's Jimmy. I was the patrolman you spoke to. I came on time to keep our promise. When you struck that match, I recognized your face as the man wanted in Chicago, but I couldn't bring myself to arrest my old friend, so I found a plain-clothes officer to do it for me.
